history.summary: DUPLICATE RECORD: this is the same temple as 1.json ('Amareswara Swamy Temple', Amaravati). The CSV town 'Guntur' is wrong — the temple is at Amaravati (Amaravathi), in the district now called Palnadu (formerly Guntur). It is the Amararama temple, one of the five sacred Pancharama Kshetras of Shiva, on the southern bank of the Krishna River, famous for its very tall (15-ft) white marble Shiva lingam — the largest of the Pancharama lingams — with a red stain said to be blood from when a nail was struck into the lingam to stop it growing. Legend says Indra installed the lingam from the broken pieces of Tarakasura's lingam. The site flourished under the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Vengi Chalukyas, was expanded by Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu, carries inscriptions of the Kota chiefs and the Vijayanagara Empire, and shows Buddhist architectural influence (Amaravati was a major Buddhist site). Its gopuram was renovated in 2017 (Rs.1.56 crore), revealing 1,800-year-old artifacts. Keep-or-remove decision needed: identical to 1.json apart from the CSV name/town.

name: Sri Amaralingeswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Amaravati (Amaravathi) is an ancient town on the southern bank of the Krishna River, about 40 km from Guntur. It was one of the great Buddhist centres of the Satavahana period (famous Mahachaitya stupa), hosts the Pancharama Shiva temple of Amareswara, and is the designated capital city of Andhra Pradesh — now in Palnadu district.

travel.airport: Nearest major airport is Vijayawada (Gannavaram), roughly 50 km away (verify).
travel.railway: No major station at Amaravati; nearest railheads are Guntur (~35 km) and Vijayawada (~55 km) (verify).
travel.road: About 40 km from Guntur; APSRTC operates regular buses from Guntur, Vijayawada and Mangalagiri to Amaravathi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Maha Shivaratri is the grandest occasion but extremely crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily, morning and evening shifts (verify on site; timings change during festivals and Karthika month).
